result.title: ADE: A Zero-Training Unlearning Method for Latent World Models
result.summary: Latent world models learn compact recurrent dynamics from offline trajectories, yet deployed simulators can retain backdoor triggers or stale transitions from outdated physical regimes. Existing unlearning methods fail in autoregressive physics: gradient updates distort latent manifolds and compound rollout drift, naive output zeroing suppresses valid control responses on trigger onset, and single-step deletion leaves corruption inside recurrent hidden states. We propose Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE), a deterministic, zero-training closed-form unlearning algorithm for latent world models. Using only cached pretraining moments, ADE recovers retain covariances via single-pass matrix downdating without raw retain data and cascades closed-form edits across the input bottleneck, hidden states, and downstream heads. Pairing orthogonal excision with whitened recurrent damping and mean-preserving affine calibration neutralizes out-of-manifold backdoors and realigns in-manifold shifts without variance collapse. Across four regimes on three MuJoCo benchmarks, ADE outperforms seven tuned baselines on DreamerV1, eliminating HalfCheetah and Hopper velocity-flip triggers $4.4\times$ faster than fine-tuning, and transfers zero-shot to DreamerV3.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 latent world model 中残留的后门触发或过时动力学，提出免训练的闭式遗忘算法 ADE：仅用缓存的预训练统计量恢复保留协方差，并在输入瓶颈、循环隐状态与输出头上级联解析编辑，配合正交切除与白化阻尼抑制 rollout 漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「闭式编辑循环隐状态、避免梯度更新破坏 latent 流形与逐步误差累积」的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中定向修改或剔除内部推理状态、以及多步状态更新稳定性的问题；但对象是控制用世界模型，与视觉推理任务距离较远，联系属推测。
